## #1 — JackOfSpades — 2010-09-23

Material Saver

It shouldn't exactly be here, because it's a plugin for the Finder, not Cheetah3D.

It's a simple tool for saving downloaded Materials without that hassle.
All you do is rightclick the .c3dmat-file and select "Save Material".
The material will be copied into a new folder named "Imported in the Material-folder.
To install, simply put the plugin into Library/Services.

Attachments: [Plugin.zip](https://www.cheetah3d.com/forum/index.php?attachments/12033/)

## #4 — frank beckmann — 2018-01-22
<https://www.cheetah3d.com/forum/index.php?threads/6267/post-110613>

[[QUOTE:  LUKO said: I have tryed it and it does not work at all ... The material appears but it is grayish and i can't select it ... I have installed the plugin as you explained it ... Click to expand... ]]
And it still works.
Once installed it will add an entry to the macOS "Services". Download the material.zip - unzip - make a right-click and go Services->Save Material. This will add a new folder into ->Application Support->Cheetah3D->Materials called "Imported". Restart Cheetah3d and go Add material->Imported->......
There you have it.

Cheers
Frank

Attachments: [SaveMaterial.png](https://www.cheetah3d.com/forum/index.php?attachments/32130/)
